name: Mattan
overview: Mattan is a male figure identified in Scripture as a priest of Baal, serving in a religious capacity opposed to the worship of the true God. His tribal affiliation and family background are not recorded, limiting details about his broader context. His role as a Baal priest places him within the spiritual conflict present in the history of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Mattan means "gift," a proper name mentioned in 2 Kings 11:18. There is no indication that this name was given by God, and it does not carry a specific theological significance beyond its literal meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Mattan beyond his role as a priest of Baal. There are no listed relatives or connections to other biblical figures.
scriptureSignificance: Mattan's significance lies in his position as a priest of Baal during a time when Israel struggled with idolatry and apostasy. His presence as a Baal priest highlights the ongoing spiritual battles and the challenges faced by God's people to remain faithful. Mattan represents the opposition to true worship that the faithful remnant had to confront.
